milestones.title: Actor support and executor architecture
milestones.ledgerEvidence: Logical cooperative-default and MainActor executor identity, source hops, caller restoration, detached-task lane identity, distinct source-actor runtime IDs, weak actor-record cleanup, canonical user-declared global-actor mapping through static shared, struct- and enum-backed arbitrary global-actor capability propagation through `#isolation` and defaulted isolated dispatch, depth-counted mailbox ownership for synchronous and async actor-function plus externally awaited synchronous computed-getter and subscript-getter segments, throwing computed-getter failure cleanup, async-throwing computed/subscript-getter success/source-error/cancellation reacquisition cleanup with caller restoration, actor computed-property and subscript-setter confinement to already-owned segments, controlled suspension release/reacquisition and actor reentrancy, task-local propagation through actor hops and suspension, retained queued actor messages after task cancellation, cross-actor throwing and cancellation-observing function hops with caller restoration, explicit plus defaulted/optional source-actor, MainActor, custom-global-actor, and nil isolated-parameter dispatch, explicit waitingForActor handoff/cleanup, replayable seeded mailbox stress with complete runtime draining, and mutable stored-property confinement with Swift-compatible immutable-let and nonisolated exceptions are covered.
milestones.ledgerRemainingWork: Active demand cycle (2026-07-16): finish per-feature fail-closed flips with no up-front global rejection; physical workers remain M9.

requirements.notes: Logical cooperative-default and MainActor hops are covered without claiming physical worker execution.

Final slice of the 2026-07-16 demand cycle: each actor semantic feature flips from the documented class-like compatibility path to fail-closed diagnosis together with or after its actor-runtime replacement. Synchronous actor initialization is characterized: its body is lexically nonisolated, may initialize stored state without await, and the first externally awaited isolated method owns the new actor mailbox. Task-local bindings are characterized as task-owned across actor entry and suspension/reacquisition, with dynamic-scope restoration and complete task/actor cleanup. A cancellation request leaves an already queued cross-actor call in the mailbox; ordinary handoff enters its method with ownership and the request remains available for cooperative observation. A global up-front rejection of valid actor declarations is forbidden while corpus and FoodTruck ratchets execute through the compatibility path. The boundary closes when every demand-scoped actor feature routes through the actor runtime and remaining unsupported actor forms are explicitly diagnosed instead of silently absorbed.

The entry slice of the 2026-07-16 demand cycle is covered. Source actor declarations retain their nominal actor kind, each instance receives a distinct runtime ID backed by a non-owning record, final release removes that record, and a collected user-declared global actor resolves through its canonical static shared identity. Synchronous and async actor-isolated functions plus externally awaited synchronous computed-property and subscript getters acquire depth-counted mailbox leases before changing logical executor; computed and subscript getters retain their declared async/throwing effects, a throwing computed getter releases the target on failure, and async-throwing computed/subscript getters reacquire their target before normal return, source-thrown error, or cancellation observation, then release it and restore their caller before subsequent caller work; computed-property and subscript setters require an already-owned actor segment because Swift rejects external mutation even when spelled with await. Canonical host/task/clock/group waits release the complete nested segment, and resumption queues on the same actor before source evaluation continues. Competing source tasks record waitingForActor, receive direct ownership handoff, and cannot release while an actor edge remains. Mutable stored-property funnels require ownership, while ordinary immutable let and explicitly nonisolated storage remain readable under the native Swift 6 rule. Exact same-source actor cases are native/interpreter GREEN in 20 repetitions without FIFO, task-start, physical-thread, or cross-actor-parallelism claims. A 64-seed replayable mailbox board varies fanout, rounds, pre-entry yield, and in-segment resume yields while proving exact mutation totals, actor ownership after every resume, complete child collection, and empty task/actor/group/scope/host-operation/scheduler registries. FoodTruckCheck, ProjectCheck, and suite ratchets must not regress.

Controlled same-source parity proves that an async actor message owns its synchronous prefix, releases the complete nested segment at a host suspension, permits a second message to mutate isolated state, and reacquires the same actor before resuming. A second exact case proves a cross-actor throwing-function hop: the callee owns its segment, releases it on error, the caller is restored before catch handling, and a later callee message retains both mutations. Gated function, async-computed-getter, and async-subscript-getter cases cancel the source task while the callee is suspended, then prove callee reacquisition before cancellation observation, balanced release, caller restoration before catch, and subsequent callee progress. A queued-call case proves that cancellation does not remove a waitingForActor edge: handoff still enters the method with actor ownership and the request remains observable. Separate source-gated async computed/subscript cases prove the same balanced target/caller transition on normal return and source-thrown error. Task-local propagation retains one task-owned binding map across actor entry, suspension, mailbox reacquisition, and dynamic-scope restoration. Isolated parameters preserve syntax metadata and select their executor from the bound runtime value before function entry. Required explicit source actors, default #isolation inherited from a source actor, MainActor, or a custom global actor, explicit source actors, explicit nil, and a nil default in nonisolated code are covered; the default is evaluated once in the caller's lexical isolation and the exact value is reused for binding. Struct- and enum-backed global-actor declarations may expose a different source-actor type as static shared; both nominal representations now preserve @globalActor metadata, resolve that exact canonical capability, and own its mailbox through nested defaulted isolated dispatch. Already-owned synchronous entry is legal, while unawaited cross-actor entry fails closed. The shared runtime path balances task, clock, host, group, accessor, and explicit executor-hop suspensions. A native-anchored exact fixture plus a 64-seed replayable stress board cover mailbox fanout, repeated rounds, suspension/reacquisition, invariant mutation totals, full child collection, and empty runtime registries without claiming FIFO or physical threads. This covers the reentrancy and isolated-dispatch slice; the per-feature actor safety boundary remains open.
